title: Daily Routine Speaking Practice
description: Learn to describe your daily routine in English using time expressions, present simple verbs and a guided speaking exercise.

body_markdown:
## 1. Talk about regular activities

Use the present simple tense to describe habits and routines.

- I wake up at six o'clock.
- I brush my teeth.
- I have breakfast.
- I leave home for work.
- I return home in the evening.
- I go to bed at night.

For he, she or it, remember the verb ending: “She wakes up early.”

## 2. Time expressions

| Expression | Example |
|---|---|
| in the morning | I exercise in the morning. |
| at noon | I have lunch at noon. |
| in the afternoon | I work in the afternoon. |
| in the evening | I study in the evening. |
| at night | I read at night. |
| every day | I practise every day. |

## 3. Sample paragraph

“I wake up early in the morning. First, I get ready and have breakfast. Then I leave home for work. I complete my daily responsibilities and return home in the evening. After dinner, I spend some time reading or learning English. I go to bed at night.”

Change the times and activities to match your real routine.

## 4. Put the activities in order

Use these words to connect your sentences: **first, then, after that, later, finally**.

Example: “First, I wake up. Then, I get ready. After that, I have breakfast.”

## 5. Practice test

Choose the correct option.

1. She ______ up at seven. (wake / wakes)
2. I ______ breakfast every day. (have / has)
3. He ______ to work by bus. (go / goes)
4. They ______ English in the evening. (study / studies)
5. I go to bed ______ night. (at / on)

**Answers:** 1. wakes, 2. have, 3. goes, 4. study, 5. at.

## 6. Speaking task

Describe your own daily routine for one minute. Include at least five activities and three time expressions. Speak naturally and use your actual routine.

faq.question: Which tense is used for daily routines?
faq.answer: The present simple tense is commonly used for habits and regular activities.

faq.question: How do I describe the order of activities?
faq.answer: Use sequence words such as first, then, after that, later and finally.

faq.question: Should I copy the sample routine exactly?
faq.answer: No. Change the times and activities so the description matches your real day.
